Graphic Designer

Educated Choices Program
“Educating for a Better World”
  • Freelance
  • Remote
  • Posted 11 hours ago
  • Educated Choices Program

Job Overview

The ECP Graphic Designer may (but is not limited to), assist with Communications department tasks, such as:

  • Visual Asset Creation: Design high-quality, clear, and engaging digital and print materials, including social media graphics, email headers, videos, landing pages, flyers, billboards, public-facing documents, and other graphic designs.
    • Edit short-form educational reels
    • Create simple motion graphics and animated text overlays
    • Typical weekly projects may include:
      • 3–5 social graphics
      • 1–2 carousel posts
      • Newsletter, blog, and PR assets
  • Brand Stewardship: Adhere to brand guidelines (color palettes, typography, and logo usage) to ensure consistency across all channels.
  • Concept Development: Collaborate with the marketing or creative team to brainstorm and execute original visual concepts for specific campaigns.

​Preferred Qualifications:​

  • Proficient in Google Workspace
  • Experience working in  Monday.com  or similar task management systems
  • Experience in Canva and Adobe Creative Cloud applications (Illustrator, Photoshop)
  • Strong and diverse design portfolio
  • Experience in the academic or nonprofit sectors
  • Ability to communicate clearly and work effectively with minimal supervision
  • Ability to freehand draw illustrations, create digital designs, and produce short videos
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Flexible and open to feedback
  • Fully bilingual in English and Spanish is a bonus
  • Experience designing for Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and YouTube
  • Understanding of carousel design strategy and engagement-driven layouts

​

Tagged as: design, media, social media, video production, content creation, graphic design, communications, brand strategy

Educated Choices Program

The Educated Choices Program (ECP) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to providing free food-related education, empowering students and community members to recognize the importance and responsibility of making informed decisions about their food, and building a healthier, more sustainable future for everyone. Offering digital presentations to students and communities across the globe, ECP has reached more than 3.5 million people in 7 languages, and we are just getting started!
